Subject: Initial redlines on Redwood DPA (SCCs + UK IDTA concerns)

Marissa —

Thanks for sending over the latest DPA. Our legal team reviewed and attached a marked-up (see Redlined_DPA_v3.docx) — key points for our side:

- We need explicit fallback language if SCCs are not accepted by a local regulator; we propose a short clause allowing temporary processing in EU-only regions until resolved.
- The UK IDTA addendum needs clarity on which subprocessor transfers are covered and whether the signature of the IDTA can be executed by DocuSign.
- Data subject rights: a small localization paragraph requested for UK residents (reference to local supervisory authority).

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can:
1) produce a SCCs/IDTA comparison table (mapping our requests to your standard clauses), and
2) run a single DocuSign envelope for the DPA + IDTA addendum (we prefer DocuSign).

We can schedule 30 minutes today or tomorrow to resolve the remaining redlines.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Counsel, FinRegCo

Liam / Marissa —

I've attached a short mapping table (SCCs_and_UK_IDTA_comparison_table.xlsx) that maps FinRegCo's requested edits to our recommended language and indicates where we can accept the change, propose alternative language, or cannot accept (with brief rationale). Highlights:

- Fallback processing: we can accept an interim "EU-only processing" operational restriction for a limited remediation period (we've proposed 30 days) while both legal teams engage regulators; we can't accept an indefinite restriction that blocks service availability for our other customers.
- UK IDTA: we can execute the IDTA via DocuSign; however, signature pages should reference the DPA version number to ensure consistent linkage.
- Subprocessor transfers: we added a clarifying paragraph that any new subprocessor added post-signature will trigger a 30-day notice with export-impact assessment.

I'll be in the call later today and can walk through line-by-line.

— Karthik

Thanks Karthik — that table is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side after internal review:

- The proposed 30-day interim window is acceptable, provided there is an explicit escalation path to a named Redwood executive for urgent remediation (so we can avoid long service interruptions). Can you add a one-line escalation contact?
- On the subprocessor notice: please confirm whether the "30-day notice" blocks transfer of data during that period or is purely informational. Our preference is the latter (informational only).

We are good with DocuSign for both documents and are aiming to have signatures executed by next week if the final markup is agreed. Please advise on the DocuSign workflow you prefer (single envelope vs separate envelopes).

Best,

Senior Counsel, FinRegCo

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — operational implications (SCCs/fallback)

Team / Emma —

Quick technical note on the proposed interim EU-only processing fallback:

- We can enforce region restriction at the tenancy level for FinRegCo (pin the account to eu-west-1 pools) within 24-48 hours of a signed change order, but some features (cross-region cache warming, global KV replication) may be degraded. We'll document expected performance implications in the export-impact assessment.
- For the 30-day notice on subprocessors: our intent is informational only — we do not automatically block transfers during a notice window. If FinRegCo requires a hard stop, that becomes an operational restriction that would need separate SOW and lead time.

I'll add a one-line escalation contact in the DPA (Director, Global Privacy Operations — privacy-ops@redwood.com) and include a short annex with expected perf impact bullet points.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy Engineering | Redwood Inference
